clue.text: Pledge offered by a company of funeral directors

definitions.meaning: a binding promise to do something
a business firm whose trade is arranging funerals

explanation.surface: A promise made by a firm of funeral directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: FIRM is a company and UNDERTAKING is the business of funeral directors, who in Britain are also called undertakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm undertaking is a solid, binding promise, and also, read literally, a business in the funeral trade.

clue.text: Journeyman identified as one of the Reds under the bed

definitions.meaning: read literally, a man making a journey with others

definitions.text: one of the Reds under the bed
definitions.meaning: a Communist sympathiser feared to be hidden in society, from the Cold War phrase 'Reds under the bed'

explanation.surface: A tradesman exposed as a hidden Communist agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds under the bed' was a Cold War scare phrase about hidden Communists; a fellow traveller was a sympathiser who was not a party member.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a companion on a journey, and figuratively a Communist sympathiser outside the party.

clue.text: Democrat initially put in racial reforms of a fundamental nature

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, so the Democrat's letter goes into the rearranged word
to reform is to reshape, so the letters of racial are rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of the word Democrat

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician brings in sweeping changes to race laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges RACIAL into RAICAL, and 'put in' sets D, the first letter of 'Democrat', inside it after RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical means going to the root of something, so it describes a basic, far-reaching nature.

clue.text: Not a new American edition

explanation.surface: This isn't a fresh printing from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-hand is not new, the opposite of fresh from the shop.

clue.text: Ruin for a British ministry going to the city of Paris

indicators.note: going to means the ministry's letters are followed directly by the city's name

parts.note: DES was the Department of Education and Science, a former British government ministry
in Greek legend Paris was the prince of Troy, so his city is Troy

explanation.surface: A government department brings disaster to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city of Paris' suggests the French capital, but this Paris is the Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen caused the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to wreck it completely, bringing it to ruin.

clue.text: Go flat out to produce record sales product

parts.note: REC is an abbreviation for record, as on a recording device
a line is a range of goods offered for sale

explanation.surface: Working at full speed to turn out a best-selling disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go flat out' looks like 'work at full speed' but means lie flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie back fully stretched is literally going flat, lying out horizontally.

clue.text: Area of land fiercely contested by the Crusaders

definitions.meaning: a measure of land, 4,840 square yards
the port in the Holy Land besieged during the Third Crusade

explanation.surface: A piece of ground bitterly fought over by the knights of the Crusades.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a unit of land measurement and the name of the Holy Land port the Crusaders besieged in 1189-91.

clue.text: Child recently born to a Spanish princess

parts.note: a baby newly born is an infant

explanation.surface: A baby has just been delivered to a royal lady of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Infanta is the title of a daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese king.

clue.text: Midas farewell to a retiring employee

definitions.text: Midas farewell to a retiring employee

parts.words: Midas farewell to a retiring employee
parts.note: King Midas turned what he touched to gold, so his parting grip would be gilded; read plainly, a large leaving payment

explanation.surface: The legendary king of gold bids goodbye to a worker leaving the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: King Midas turned everything he touched into gold, so his farewell would be a gilded clasp of the hand; the phrase means a generous payoff to someone leaving a company.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names a big lump-sum payment given to a departing executive or retiree.

clue.text: They can be climbed by large snakes

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
adders are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: In the board game, these are what take you up past the big serpents.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the board game Snakes and Ladders, but 'large snakes' splits into L and ADDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladders are things one climbs, rung by rung.

clue.text: Precise about seeing that the motor has fresh fuel

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new form, so the letters of fuel are mixed afresh

explanation.surface: Being particular about checking that the car has been given new petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges FUEL into EFUL, which follows CAR; 'about seeing that' and 'has' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful worker is exact and meticulous.

clue.text: Cry of pain heard in Oxford University church

explanation.surface: A yelp of hurt rings out in a college chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is what someone shouts when suddenly hurt.

clue.text: A tiny bit of mottling in the wood

definitions.meaning: a minute particle, as of sand or salt
the pattern of fibres visible in timber

explanation.surface: A small speck of figuring in a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a minute particle and the fibrous pattern seen in timber.

clue.text: Cook needs a slice of the joint

indicators.note: a slice is a part cut from the whole, so the answer is a run taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A chef requires a portion of the roast meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a roast of meat, but it is a joint of the body; the letters run across 'cooK NEEds'.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Stay on a tender note

parts.note: a tender is an offer, as is a bid
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Remain on a gentle musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' reads as gentle but is the noun, a formal offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or dwell somewhere.

clue.text: Serve up a drink fit for a king

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: lager is a light beer

explanation.surface: Pour a beverage worthy of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve up' turns LAGER upward, giving its letters backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, befitting a monarch.

clue.text: The chest of long, lanky lad

parts.note: a long, lanky person is tall
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: The torso of a gangling youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests the body, but it is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a high chest of drawers, often in two stacked sections.

clue.text: A lotion to relieve conjunctivitis? Bunkum!

definitions.meaning: a liquid for rinsing sore eyes
nonsense, claptrap

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an eye-drop remedy as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a soothing liquid for the eyes and a slang word for nonsense or humbug.

clue.text: Leave a lot of players playing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
on means taking part, as a player on the field is on

explanation.surface: Quit a whole crowd of performers mid-show.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or walk away from.

clue.text: Not quite all there? That's rather unfair

definitions.meaning: slightly mad or eccentric
a remark that something is somewhat out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is a bit dim, and they protest that the jibe is unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means slightly odd in the head, and also somewhat improper or unfair.

clue.text: Unable to compete since the game's been cancelled

definitions.meaning: outclassed, not equal to a rival
read literally, there is no fixture today

explanation.surface: A team can't play because the fixture is off.
explanation.definitionFit: It means being outclassed by a rival, and literally that no game will take place.

clue.text: Those who are late find only emptied bottles

definitions.meaning: the dead, the late departed
slang for drained bottles after a party

explanation.surface: People who turn up late find only empties left.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a term for the deceased and slang for empty bottles left after drinking.

clue.text: A spider changed this emotion in Robert the Bruce

definitions.text: this emotion in Robert the Bruce

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the phrase are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A spider altered the King of Scots' mood of hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Robert the Bruce, King of Scots, hiding in despair, took heart from a spider's repeated tries at spinning a web; here 'changed' rearranges A SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, the mood the legend gives Bruce before the spider inspired him.

clue.text: A man of the sea. Right?

definitions.text: A man of the sea. Right?

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they have correctly called a person a seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a sailor, a seaman.

clue.text: Former spouse takes Italian vermouth as the way out

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in the cocktail gin and it

explanation.surface: An ex-husband grabs a Martini and heads for the door.
explanation.walkthrough: In a 'gin and it' the IT is Italian vermouth, a British bar convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a door or route by which one leaves.

clue.text: Inappropriately made for a single woman

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Something unsuitably tailored for an unmarried lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrongly or out of place.

clue.text: The arguments in favour of salaried sportsmen

definitions.meaning: points for, as in 'the ... and cons'
professionals, paid players

explanation.surface: The case for paying athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both points in favour and paid professional players.

clue.text: Do the French give unemployment benefit?

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Do people in France hand out jobless pay?
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the dole is everyday slang for state unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dole is the British informal term for welfare paid to the jobless.

clue.text: Laos is partitioned too

indicators.note: a country partitioned is split up and redrawn, so the letters of Laos are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Asian country is also divided.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition, as well.

clue.text: Cave is an observation post

definitions.meaning: Latin for beware, used as a schoolboy warning cry
a place for keeping watch

explanation.surface: A cavern serves as a watching point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' is not a cavern: it is the Latin 'beware', the warning a British schoolboy lookout would hiss.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a shouted warning to beware and a position for keeping watch.

clue.text: Greek female runner suffers a loss in Georgia

indicators.note: suffering a loss means the name has one of its letters, an A, taken away

parts.note: Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek myth who raced her suitors

explanation.surface: A Greek woman athlete is defeated in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers a loss' looks like a defeat in a race; it removes one A from ATALANTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: A pub-crawl of educational value to the mature student?

definitions.text: A pub-crawl of educational value to the mature student?

parts.words: A pub-crawl of educational value to the mature student?
parts.note: a round of drinks, or refreshers, taken in sequence, read as a training programme to update skills

explanation.surface: A drinking tour passed off as adult education.
explanation.walkthrough: A refresher is slang for a drink, so a tour of pubs is a 'course' of them; the real phrase means a short training course to update knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: This names a short course updating the skills of someone already qualified.
